    Axels¶

    The human sub-race of North Erisdar. Axels are typically taller and blond — a physical profile shaped by the northern climate and generations of relative isolation from southern populations. Culturally analogous to the Norse peoples of Old Earth.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: Tall (1.75–1.95m average for men), fair-skinned, with predominantly blond or light brown hair. Blue and gray eyes are common. Broad-shouldered and robust — built for cold climates
    • Lifespan: 60–75 years
    • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Northern mages tend toward storm-calling and frost magic — practical abilities for a harsh climate
    • Cold adaptation: Higher metabolic rates and denser body hair than southern humans. Axels can work outdoors in temperatures that would incapacitate a Baothian

    Society¶

    Axel society is clan-based and martial, organized around longhouses and coastal settlements. The northern climate demands cooperation — an isolated family does not survive the winter.

    • Governance: Jarldoms — regional chieftains who swear fealty to a high king in times of war. Day-to-day, each jarl rules their fjord or valley with considerable autonomy
    • Culture: Oral tradition is sacred. Axel skalds memorize genealogies stretching back millennia. A well-told saga at a winter feast is worth more than gold. Shipbuilding is the highest art — Axel longships are feared and respected across the northern seas
    • Religion: Pre-Erisian animism persists in remote areas — spirits of storm, sea, and mountain. The Erisian church has made significant inroads but the old ways die hard in the north
    • Values: Strength, loyalty to clan, and a good death. Axels do not fear dying — they fear dying without their deeds being remembered

    Language¶

    • Primary: Axel (originated in Northaxeland)
    • Secondary: Baothian

    Connections¶

    • Region: North Erisdar
    • Nations: Northaxeland, Cossiland, , Kent, Tetras, Venkradian Republic
    • Appearance: Tall, blond, fair-skinned
    • Cultural analog: Viking / Norse
